senses.gloss: ch. sameto be blunt (and loose); to be dull, faint.
units: <cite ref="Targum Jerusalem, Genesis 33:4">Targ. Y. II, Gen. XXXIII, 4</cite> (Y. I <he>אתמזמיזו</he>). Ib. XXXII, 26 <he>וקהת</he> (some ed. <he>וקחת</he>, v. <cite ref="S00683"><he>קְחַח</he></cite>; Y. I <he>זעזע</he>; h. text <he>ותקע</he>).—[<cite ref="Targum Jonathan on I Kings 14:4">Targ. I Kings XIV, 4</cite> <he>קהאה</he> (ed. Wil. <he>כהאה</he>; ed. Lag. <cite ref="S01439"><he>קמא</he></cite>; h. text <he>קמו</he>.]

Ber. 56ᵃ קהא עסקך וכ׳ Ms. F. (ed. קָאוֵי fr. קְוָא; Ms. M. פסיד עסקך וקאזיל, read וקאוי) thy business (wine store) will be stale (and taste) like a pomegranate.—Part. pass. קְהִיהַ, pl. קְהִיתִין (cmp. חֲמִי, a. חַמְת׳).
<cite ref="Vayikra Rabbah 19:4">Lev. R. s. 19</cite> <he>הא קהיתין</he> are they (the vessels with wine you have been examining) spoiled?; [Ar. s. v. <he>קה</he>: <he>הָקְהֵיתָה</he> is it spoiled?].

<cite ref="Bava Metzia 52b:10">B. Mets. 52ᵇ</cite> <he>דקָהֵי אזוזי מקרי נפש רעה</he> Ar. (ed. <he>דמוקים</he>) he who is rigorous in matters of coins (refusing a coin for slight imperfections) is called ‘a malevolent soul’ (v. <cite ref="N01084"><he>נֶפֶשׁ</he></cite>).
<cite ref="Pesachim 116a:3">Pes. 116ᵃ</cite> <he>צריך לְקַהוּיֵיה</he> one must give the pap (<cite ref="H01630"><he>חֲרוֹסֶת</he></cite>) an acrid taste (with apples and wine).

senses.gloss: [to blunt a person’s teeth,] to refute, argue.
units: <cite ref="Yevamot 110b">Yeb. 110ᵇ</cite> <he>מַקְהוּ</he> Ar. a. Var. in Rashi (ed. <he>מַקְווּ</he>), v. <cite ref="A02897"><he>אַקְוָוא</he></cite>.
